label: The President Stays In
detail: The President does not withdraw, and remains the nominee of the party that has held the White House since 2021 through election day.
assumption: The nominee on the Democratic line is the 82-year-old incumbent President rather than his actual replacement; his age and debate performance weigh on voters' views, and baseline party loyalty and turnout shift accordingly.
facts_text: The vice president remains the running mate on the ticket of the party that has held the White House since 2021.
Polls in the weeks before election day show many voters concerned about the President's age.
nominee_news: The President ended speculation about his candidacy and said he would stay in the race and remain the nominee of the party that has held the White House since 2021.
He has faced calls from some members of his own party to step aside after a widely criticized debate performance in June.
research_questions: How did voters behave when an incumbent president seen as too old or infirm stayed on the ticket, as with Woodrow Wilson's illness in 1920 or Franklin Roosevelt's health in 1944?
How did turnout and party loyalty change when a party's nominee faced open doubts from within his own party?
How did voters respond when an incumbent party changed its nominee late versus kept its nominee?
source_text: Joe Biden stays in the 2024 race as the Democratic nominee.
